import datetime,hashlib,json,os,pathlib,subprocess,time
root=pathlib.Path.home()/'build/ckutilities-files-20261023-01a165ae'
os.environ['TMPDIR']=str(root/'tmp')
fixture=root/'fscrypt-fixture-20261024'
if fixture.exists(): raise SystemExit('Private fixture root already exists')
fixture.mkdir()
records=[]
def run(label,command):
 start=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat();tick=time.monotonic()
 p=subprocess.run(command,stdout=subprocess.PIPE,stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,text=True)
 rec=dict(label=label,command=command,start=start,end=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(),elapsed_seconds=round(time.monotonic()-tick,3),exit_code=p.returncode,output=p.stdout)
 records.append(rec);(root/'wp01-fscrypt-fixture-prepare.json').write_text(json.dumps(dict(root=str(fixture),steps=records),indent=2)+'\n')
 print(json.dumps(rec),flush=True)
 if p.returncode: raise SystemExit(p.returncode)
def sudo(command):return ['sudo','-n','env','TMPDIR='+str(root/'tmp'),*command]
run('prebuild-owners',['sh','-c','ps -eo pid,comm,args | sed -n "1p"'])
run('compile-private-helper',['cc','-std=c11','-D_GNU_SOURCE','-Wall','-Wextra','-Werror',str(root/'wp01-fscrypt-prepare.c'),'-o',str(fixture/'prepare')])
fd=os.open(fixture/'image.ext4',os.O_CREAT|os.O_EXCL|os.O_WRONLY,0o600);os.ftruncate(fd,64*1024*1024);os.close(fd)
(fixture/'mount').mkdir()
run('format-private-image',['mkfs.ext4','-q','-F','-O','encrypt',str(fixture/'image.ext4')])
run('mount-private-image',sudo(['mount','-o','loop,nodev,nosuid,noexec',str(fixture/'image.ext4'),str(fixture/'mount')]))
run('record-mount',['findmnt','--target',str(fixture/'mount'),'--json','--output','SOURCE,FSTYPE,TARGET,OPTIONS'])
run('private-root-ownership',sudo(['chown',str(os.getuid())+':'+str(os.getgid()),str(fixture/'mount')]))
(fixture/'mount/encrypted').mkdir(mode=0o700)
run('set-locked-private-policy',sudo([str(fixture/'prepare'),str(fixture/'mount/encrypted')]))
print('Fixture ready',str(fixture/'mount'),flush=True)

guarantees: The product query only reads FS_IOC_GET_ENCRYPTION_POLICY_EX through the held directory descriptor. No pathname reopen, enumeration cursor changes, content read, policy assignment, key operation, privilege enablement or legacy ioctl fallback.
Only native ENODATA establishes no fscrypt policy, preserving its native witness. Unsupported kernels/drivers/platforms, unknown versions/oversize replies and native failures cannot become absence.

Fresh directory kind/identity qualification and optional known statx encryption-bit corroboration bracket successful/absent replies. Changed/unqualified contexts and contradictory bits cannot yield available reports.

Exact v1/version-0 12-byte and v2/version-2 24-byte layouts retain all mode/flag/reserved/key-reference bytes using bounded copies and native ABI assertions. Structural fields are not crypto-strength, key availability or replay claims.

An ordinary guest user successfully queried a locked v2 directory with an absent key on a private encrypt-enabled ext4 image, retained its exact bytes/ID after pathname replacement, observed ENODATA on the replacement and saw encrypted-directory name-rule refusal. No encrypted content was created or copied.
limitations: Directory-only fscrypt namespace; no whole-volume/dm-crypt/FileVault/EFS, regular-file policy, unlock-state or full preservation capability claim. Those remain required work.

Reports are live metadata observations, not snapshots, current-name proof, creation permission or execution-time preservation guarantees. Queries can block and must run on workers; later execution must qualify again.

Native positive policy coverage is v2 on the private Linux ext4 fixture. v1 and malformed/future representations have deterministic decoding coverage only. Other Linux drivers, other crypto systems and encrypted-data copying are not qualified by these fixtures.

No macOS LeakSanitizer coverage is claimed. WP-01 remains open for remaining inventories, complete native policy/capability/preservation assessment, large views, UI/worker ownership and execution safety. WP-02..08 remain required.
